text:
marie: FYI saw a p50->p99 divergence on embeds/rerank this morning after the canary deploy, non-chat workload. p50 stable, p99 spiking to ~2.1s. link to perf dashboard: https://dash.internal/r/embeds/p99 :eyes:
alex: ugh. do we have kernel flip in that canary? which model variant was used?
sasha: canary used quantized-v2 + fallback chain to cpu-hosted when GPU full. I think kernel selector favored matmul-async path.
marie: yes, kernel selector picked the new matmul-async on a subset of requests. profiler shows increased stall during KV cache lookup for short queries. attaching snippet from perf-bot:
perf-bot: ````
PROFILE SUMMARY (1727600000)
endpoint: embeds/rerank
workload: non-chat (avg tokens 18)
median_latency: 82ms
p95_latency: 420ms
p99_latency: 2100ms
gpu_util: 67%
hotspots: kernel:matmul-async (45%), kv-lookup (18%), scheduling overhead (12%)
````
ken: the kv-lookup number is interesting. were we hitting KVCACHE misses or expensive deserialization?
li: i pulled a flamegraph from the node that saw the p99s: most time spent waiting on kvcache lock + copying small tensors back to host before kernel. seems like small-batch case thrashes the cache lookups.
sasha: that matches our earlier hypothesis: continuous batching for non-chat (short queries) is forming lots of tiny batches -> kernel selection switches to async matmul that favors large matrices but incurs overhead for many tiny invocations.
alex: proposal: introduce a "slotting" policy for embed/rerank non-chat that biases batch formation to prefer token-budget fill over request-count thresholds for small-token requests. basically hold a micro-window (~12ms) and fill up to token_budget or 32 requests, whichever comes first.
marie: sounds good. do we have a config snippet we can test in staging?
ken: here's a draft change to batching config (staging only):
````json
{
  "queue_policy": "slotting_pulse",
  "micro_window_ms": 12,
  "token_budget": 800,   // tokens per micro-window
  "max_requests": 32,
  "early_fill_threshold": 0.6
}
````
li: note token_budget 800 chosen because avg tokens 18 * ~30 reqs ~= 540 tokens, gives headroom and avoids tiny matmul path. also set early_fill to avoid head-of-line stalls when traffic tails off.
sasha: also add kernel affinity hint so kernel selector prefers baseline dense-kernel for batches <512 tokens total to avoid matrmul-async overhead. We can expose hint without forcing it permanently.
marie: good. what's the testing plan? regressions to watch for?
alex: test matrix: baseline vs slotting_pulse with quantized-v2, with/without kvprefetch, low QPS bursty traffic, and steady QPS. Measure p50/p95/p99, token-per-second throughput, and GPU occupancy.
ken: I'll wire a short replay traffic job that mimics production non-chat client traces and run 3 iterations in staging.
li: also run profiler with kvcache instrumentation to see miss rate and lock contention. add a histogram for batch sizes and kernel chosen.
marie: any objections to landing the config in staging today?
sasha: none from me. just watch for throughput regressions on large-batch customers (we're changing policy only for the reranker embed endpoint, and only for non-chat path).
alex: I'll add a guard: policy applied only when request.payload.type=="embed_rerank" && avg_tokens < 60.
perf-bot: load job scheduled: replay-embed-nonchat-2026-05-05-12z -> job id rj-4729
marie: perfect. ken/ali run the first iteration and paste the p99 numbers here when done. :thumbsup:
ken: running now, ETA ~10m.
li: small note: if we see improved p99 but worse p50, we may be over-buffering; we can tune micro_window down to 8ms or lower the token_budget.
marie: agreed. iterative. thanks team.
ken: first run done: staging p50=90ms, p95=430ms, p99=480ms -> big improvement on p99. batch size histogram shows mode at 18 reqs, total tokens ~324. kernel chosen baseline-dense 92% of batches.
alex: great! any impact on throughput?
ken: throughput within 3% of baseline, GPU occupancy slightly higher but <5% diff. kvcache miss rate down 40%.
li: promising. schedule another run with bursty trace and quantized-fallback chain enabled.
marie: ok schedule it. we'll keep the experiment running through the day and revert if any customer regressions pop. thanks all.
